the poor are not benefiting from the MPAs, and that the poor are breaking the rules of the MPAs.

the following questions: How do the poor perceive marine protected areas?
how the management of MPAs can help to reduce poverty and how MPAs can be designed to achieve both conservation and development objectives.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impacts of MPAs on the lives of the people living in the study sites are mixed.
poverty is a serious problem in the study sites, but that the impact on the MPA programs is variable.
the impacts of MPAs on poverty alleviation in the study sites are mixed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MPA programs have been most successful where there has been a strong commitment to the long-term sustainability of the programs, where the programs have had the greatest investment of time, where there have been the greatest investments of financial resources, where the MPA management plans have included a strong development and poverty component, and where there have been a strong sense of community ownership and participation.
poverty alleviation and MPA management can be compatible, but that there must be a strong and sustained commitment to both.
MPAs are not a magic wand to solve all of the problems of the poor, but they can make a difference in the lives of the people living near them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
poverty alleviation is a key to success of MPA programs.
MPAs can make a difference in the lives of poor people, but only if they are well designed and implemented.

the effectiveness of MPAs depends on how they are implemented and managed, and that the effectiveness of MPA implementation and management depends on the extent to which they are able to reduce poverty.
